correctness.rationale: The two labeled graphs have 9 and 12 vertices. Exact enumeration of every subset (512 and 4096 total) proves minimum sizes four and five, and finds 81 and 120 minima. From these, exchanging exactly one vertex produces full transition graphs. Direct breadth-first search and complete coordinate witnesses verify every model-component edge; an independent C++ program reproduces sizes and component tallies. No infinite extrapolation is made.

value.rationale: The first two members of a historically studied toroidal location problem give a natural first local-mobility boundary. The exact ten-component split at the smallest nonsquare toroidal member, despite a connected unrestricted exchange graph, supplies topologically meaningful graph types (four products and six cycles), not just a known scalar minimum or arbitrary count. It gives a precise example of physical monitor-relocation obstructions and a baseline for larger products.
